source.branch: During ordinary play, a successful maybe_generate_rnd_mon gate calls makemon(NULL, 0, 0, NO_MM_FLAGS). makemon() selects a common species through rndmonst(), checks goodpos(), then enters the shared creation and inventory lifecycle. The accepted C trace selects PM_ETTIN. JavaScript selects the same species but assertSupportedSpecies rejects it: its ordinary reservoir is capped at difficulty 9 and its S_GIANT class does not make is_giant true for this Ettin.
callers: allmain.c:moveloop_core -> maybe_generate_rnd_mon -> makemon(NULL, 0, 0, NO_MM_FLAGS); js/allmain.js:finishElapsedTurn -> maybe_generate_rnd_mon -> makemon_runtime.
makemon.c:makemon random-species branch -> rndmonst -> goodpos -> shared creation lifecycle; js/makemon_create.js:makemon random-species branch -> rndmonst -> assertSupportedSpecies.
dependencies: makemon.c:rndmonst and rndmonst_adj choose the source-valid species using level difficulty and weighted reservoir sampling.

makemon.c:makemon calls m_initweap, m_initinv, and m_dowear for inventory-enabled creation. The existing JavaScript Ettin weapon branch and inventory behavior are source-pinned; the regression is the earlier runtime species refusal.

nethack-c/upstream/src/allmain.c:162-167 gates a random creation with rn2(25), rn2(50), or rn2(70) and then calls makemon(NULL, 0, 0, NO_MM_FLAGS); moveloop_core calls it at lines 236-239. js/allmain.js:418-444 uses the same gate and arguments, and finishElapsedTurn calls it at lines 833-840.

nethack-c/upstream/src/makemon.c:1220-1231 handles a null ptr by calling rndmonst() and retrying only for throws_rocks/Sokoban or goodpos. There is no species allowlist there. rndmonst() delegates to rndmonst_adj() at lines 1654-1671, which uses the current level difficulty to form the selectable pool.

js/makemon_create.js:3013-3017 picks through rndmonst() and then calls assertSupportedSpecies(). The check at lines 1047-1053 admits the ordinary reservoir only through difficulty 9; its separate true-giant clause at lines 1112-1116 excludes Ettin because the species does not satisfy is_giant. This is a JavaScript support guard, not a C makemon branch.

The source has an explicit Ettin initialization path: makemon.c:m_initweap at lines 179-185 gives S_GIANT Ettins a CLUB and skips the non-Ettin rn2(5) gate. js/makemon_create.js:1832-1848 already matches it, and scripts/makemon-create.test.mjs:6236-6282 pins the Ettin inventory behavior. makemon.c:1441-1445 invokes m_initweap, m_initinv, and m_dowear in the common creation lifecycle.

The exact C-to-JS cause is established by the saved evaluation stop and the matching PM_ETTIN rejection. A minimal general correction is to admit the already-supported Ettin runtime species through the existing guard and verify the admitted replay; later first mismatches, if any, remain separate findings.
After the Ettin admission change, `node scripts/synthetic-range-evidence.mjs .cache/task-evidence.json` verified the admitted v45 segment 0 through zero-based step 90 against the C recording.

Its first remaining divergence is at one-based segment 1, step 92: C calls rn2(3) from xkilled(mon.c:3574), while JavaScript calls rn2(6); the first screen and cursor mismatches are also at boundary 92. Replaying the 91-key prefix leaves JS level.flags.has_morgue=true but level.flags.graveyard=false. This is the concrete downstream reason LEVEL_SPECIFIC_NOCORPSE skips its graveyard-undead draw for the demilich. It is a separate mklev finalization boundary, recorded for follow-up rather than included in this makemon fix.
